source.title: Universal Sparse Autoencoders: Interpretable Cross-Model Concept Alignment
source.authors: Harrish Thasarathan; J. Forsyth; Thomas Fel; Matthew Kowal; K. Derpanis

record.tranche_reason: The study tests cross-model shared representations using a shared sparse-autoencoder concept space, reconstruction, and concept-firing measures rather than the original Platonic-representation measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper tests concept alignment across three vision models and the reconstruction of one model's activations from another model's shared code. It does not sweep model size or capability, compare paired image and language representations, or train multiple seeds of the same architecture. It compares ImageNet with two out-of-distribution datasets. The cross-reconstruction matrix values are not stated in text; only the described off-diagonal positivity and relative diagonal performance are recorded. Hyperparameter sweeps are mentioned as a way to select settings, but their values are not reported as results.
record.test_reason: The study jointly trains a sparse autoencoder across DinoV2, SigLIP and ViT, three vision models with different objectives. It measures cross-model reconstruction (V4), concept co-firing and firing entropy across models (V5, V7), and whether these trends persist out of distribution (V6). This is a different method aimed at the shared-representation question. One caveat: the shared code is imposed by the training objective, so some of the measured universality may be built in by the method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that USAEs learn a shared concept space that reconstructs all three vision models' activations. Many concepts are both universal and highly important. DinoV2, and also SigLIP, encode unique features. Universal training recovers part of the independent SAEs' concepts and finds new shared ones.
record.recipe_differences: The study jointly trains TopK sparse autoencoders with a shared sparse code and model-specific decoders, and evaluates reconstruction, firing, and concept overlap. It does not reproduce either original source's method. It trains on final-layer activations from three vision models.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction and concept measurements vary by model and evaluation dataset. The study notes sensitivity to hyperparameters when increasing the number of models, but does not report the sweep results.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept co-firing frequency correlates with reconstruction energy: r=0.63 over all concepts, and r=0.89 for concepts with more than 1000 co-fires.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The most important features of a model are the most widely shared across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Only 23–38% of USAE concepts match the same model's independent SAE at cosine similarity above 0.5, against 0% for a random baseline. The overlap is higher for top co-firing concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concepts found by joint cross-model dictionary learning only partly coincide with those found per model.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: Only three vision models are tested, and all USAEs are trained on ImageNet. Cross-model reconstruction matrix values are presented in a figure without numerical values in the text. The concept-alignment evidence partly relies on qualitative examples and figure-only distributions. No model-size or capability sweep, uncertainty estimates, or same-architecture seed comparison is reported.

untested.parts: No sweep of scale or capability.
No comparison of paired image and text representations; only SigLIP's vision tower is used.
Linear maps, layer stitching, relative representations, and mapping without paired data are not tested. Only a jointly trained shared sparse code is tested.
Neurons and circuits are not tested, nor are non-vision or language models. Only the final layer is used.
Alternative similarity measures, neighbour counts and other metric settings are not varied. Cross-model reconstruction out of distribution is not reported.
Whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment is not tested; the authors' attribution of DinoV2's unique concepts to its objective is speculative. Plateau with scale is not tested.

missing.what: Numeric cross-reconstruction R² matrix, readable in the text: SigLIP row 0.61/0.36/0.25, DinoV2 row 0.31/0.77/0.31, ViT row 0.30/0.45/0.59. Rows r1–r9 record it as figure-only.
Overall mean co-fire proportion of 0.312 across the three models.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstated V4: it labelled the off-diagonal rows observed and 'supports' without the numbers, which show large loss relative to self-reconstruction. Table 1 rows measure autoencoder fidelity, not alignment. The USAE-to-independent-SAE rows compare within one model. The shared-code training objective biases the results toward finding universality.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep or comparison of model size or capability; the three vision models are compared at one stated setup.

SigLIP is included as a vision-language model, but the study does not compare representations from its image and language encoders on paired images and captions, or test alignment as both modalities improve.
No comparison of networks with the same architecture trained from different initializations.

Tests a shared sparse-code representation and decoder-based reconstruction, not linear maps between independently trained model activations, layer stitching, relative representations, or mappings without paired data.
Tests recurring visual concepts across three vision models, not recurrence of specific neurons, circuits, or SAE features across other model families or modalities.
Tests ImageNet-trained concepts on two out-of-distribution datasets and compares MSE with R²; does not vary neighbour count or systematically compare alternative similarity measures or settings.
Reports incomplete overlap and model-specific concepts, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment plateaus with scale.
